# 08-fresco — sources

Back-test entry `08-fresco.yaml`: Fresco, the AI scribe for construction superintendents (YC Fall 2024).
Written 2026-10-22 from public material only. Quotes are verbatim from the page named; "Author's choice" marks the
smallest plausible choice made where the public material is silent.

Main sources:
- [HN] Launch HN: Fresco (YC F24), 2024-11-21 — https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=42204939
- [LYC] Launch YC: Fresco, the scribe for construction, 2024-10-23 — https://www.ycombinator.com/launches/M73-fresco-the-scribe-for-construction
- [YCP] YC company page — https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/fresco (now "AI-powered takeoff and estimating for Division 8 construction")
- [KOE] A contractor's daily-log expectations on Procore's support site — https://support.procore.com/tc/Koester/Site_Map/Koester_Expectations_-_Daily_Logs
- [SWI] Swiftask, Procore daily reports page (vendor) — https://swiftask.ai/ai-integration/procore/intelligent-daily-reports
- [BLS] BLS Occupational Outlook, construction managers — https://www.bls.gov/ooh/management/construction-managers.htm
- [OPU] Launch HN: Opusense (field reports for site inspectors), 2025-05-20 — https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=44042791

## The eight founder-emulation items

1. **Who.** Construction superintendents on commercial jobs.
   [HN] "Superintendents are the busiest and most expensive people on construction sites."
   [LYC] "That’s the reality for 210k+ construction superintendents (or supervisors, foremen, PMs, etc.) across the USA."
   → `roles[superintendent]`, `context.actor`, `actor_plural`. Author's choice: "on commercial jobs" (the founders ask
   for introductions to commercial general contractors in [LYC]).

2. **What (the job).** Keep the record of the day's work, for liability and disputes.
   [HN] "30-200 photos per day to document site progress (mostly for liability reasons, or in case of a dispute with the
   owner over delays and deliverables)"; photos used to create "daily logs", "structured documents that account for the
   work done on site on any given day". [KOE] the log is "a critical piece of documentation in the arbitration of a
   dispute". → `statements.problem`, `context.job`, `interpretations.problem`.

3. **When / where.** At the end of the day, after the site walks, in the trailer.
   [HN] "At the end of the day, they'll spend a few hours uploading those photos into OneDrive, or project management
   software like Procore or ACC." [YCP] "We were curious what superintendents were doing for hours in their trailers at
   the end of the day." [LYC] "supes are spending up to 3 hours a day creating documents". → `context.circumstance`, `occasion: daily log`.
   Author's choice: the recall window {5, WORKING_DAYS} and Frequency 4 to 5 working days out of 5 (the posts say "per
   day"; a five-day site week is assumed). Prevalence `p_80_100` ("Nearly all") follows from the same "per day".

4. **Which people (the comparable group).** Superintendents at US general contractors whose jobs run on Procore or ACC.
   [LYC] "210k+ construction superintendents ... across the USA"; "Project management tools like Procore and ACC have
   dramatically increased documentation requirements". [YCP] "driving to Napa, South Bay, and around SF". → `context.segment`,
   `market: US`.

5. **Who pays.** The general contractor, per site.
   [HN] "we charge per site per month, which includes unlimited users on any given construction project".
   → `persona.decision_maker: {role: contractor}`, the BUYER role. Author's choice: the decider is the contractor's
   "operations lead" and the role to test is "The CFO" (a second role, "The project executive", listed); Purchase
   friction's three steps ("A trial on one live job" tested, a Procore check, a security review) and Commitment's step
   "start a paid pilot on one site" are the author's. Public material names no buyer title; [LYC] asks for
   introductions to general contractors by firm, not by role.

6. **Mechanism.** Narrated short videos turned into notes, texted to the crew, pushed to Procore/ACC.
   [HN] "Supers simply take short videos with voiceover, or upload photos, and Fresco does the rest, creating notes with
   transcription, photos, assignees, and due dates. Supers can easily text their crew action items, and receive texts
   back". "We also route this to whatever project management software they're using with a single click."
   [LYC] the narrated example "The beam in the southwest corner of room 134 is corroded and needs replacement by Alex.";
   "Supes who use Fresco complete their notes, on average, 90% faster."
   → `statements.solution`, `solution_mechanism`, Compatibility and Adoption friction items. Relative advantage's two
   benefits are from [HN] ("during their site walks, not after") and [LYC] ("90% faster"); their wording is the author's.

7. **Price.** About $1k per site per month, less with multi-site or multi-month terms.
   [HN] "The typical price is $1k/month, but we offer discounts for multi-month or multi-site commitments."
   → `commercial.price` {800, 1000, month}. Author's choice: the low end of $800 stands for the stated discounts.
   Existing sacrifice: 30 to 60 hours a month per site at an hourly rate of 55 — from [LYC] "up to 3 hours a day" and
   [HN] "a few hours uploading", taken as 1.5 to 3 hours on about twenty working days (author's arithmetic). The rate is
   [BLS] "$55.28 per hour" (median, construction managers, May 2025), the author's stand-in: no superintendent wage is
   in the public material. Ability to pay is derived by code (24% to 61%).

8. **Occasions.** The narrated beam; a school refit report; the uploads and logs at the end of the day.
   [LYC] on a school refit walkthrough: "Normally, creating the final report takes 2+ hours."
   [HN] "few supers have time to do this thoroughly, so these photos aren't very searchable." No named customer quote
   exists in public; the occasions below are scripted from these and from practitioner comments.

No respondent carries the name of a commenter, customer or founder.

## Open
- The verdict was scripted to be plausible and not obviously "build": the problem holds on how often but people
  disagree on whether the log is one of their two worst difficulties; the solution splits on the benefit and on
  talking over videos on site; the price fails (two of eight at the founder's band or above) while the cost it would
  replace is above the price. This is the author's reading of the thread's sceptics, not a measured result.
- No public account names a buyer title at a general contractor; the decider, the tested role "The CFO", the purchase
  steps and the Commitment step are the author's.
- hourly_rate 55 is a proxy (construction managers, not superintendents).
- Existing sacrifice picks use `period: quarter` (the corpus's convention), although the registry's recall period for a
  monthly cost reads "last month"; the values are the monthly figures times three.
- The window {5, WORKING_DAYS} is the author's; the public posts say "per day".

screens.why1: Right after I typed what Fresco does better than today's way, this is the obvious place for Keel to show me my benefits back and the belief it will test.
screens.why2: Hours back at the end of the day and action items to the crew are how supers and I talk; nothing here needs a second read.
screens.why3: These are the two gains I pitch every supe on (time in the trailer and getting punch items to the crew), so I can judge them straight from my own customers.
screens.why4: Two distinct rows, one gain each, no overlap, within the 9-word limit, and 'I'm not sure' isn't needed here.
screens.why5: It keeps my 90%-faster and texting-the-crew claims, said as hours back and same-day action items, without inventing a number I didn't write.
screens.why7: The rows meet the shape and the bar can be supported or refuted, but the hard case (a day spent uploading photos in the trailer) is close to every supe's routine rather than one day that went wrong, and same-day action items only loosely follows from an uploading day, since many supes already tell the crew on the walk.
screens.instead: Keep 'Hours back at the end of the day' and replace the second row with 'Notes done during the walk, not after', tested against their last day the log ran into the evening.

screens.why1: After the fit with today's work and the advantage, asking what effort my supers would have to take on to start is the obvious next question about the idea.
screens.why2: 'Setup, extra steps or learning' and 'start using it' are plain to me, and the four-items, nine-words limit is clear on first read.
screens.why3: I know exactly what a super would have to change on the walk and before the log goes out, because that is the product I built around their day.
screens.why4: This is a box to type in with one escape chip, and 'I'm not sure' is the right way out for a founder who can't name the efforts, since it leaves the dimension out.
screens.why5: My two efforts are kept in my words and in my voice ('they film', 'the notes'), with nothing reworded or added.
screens.why7: Both rows are base-form efforts the super takes themselves, each within nine words in the 'they' voice: one is the new habit of use on the walk, the other is the review before notes go out, which is one effort, not a bundle. Neither repeats Compatibility's 'talk over the noise' or Purchase friction's ground.

screens.why1: Right after I said what supers have to do to start, this screen shows me Keel's draft of those steps to check, which is the obvious next move.
screens.why2: 'Name who owns each item as they film' and 'check and fix the notes before they go out' are how a super talks about punch items and the notes going to the crew; the intro repeats the title, but nothing needs a second read.
screens.why3: Both are things a super does on their own walk and in their own trailer: calling out who owns the corroded beam, then reading over the notes before they text the crew or push them to Procore.
screens.why4: Two distinct efforts, one during the walk and one after it, in my words, with neither overlapping the other or Compatibility's 'talk over the noise'.
screens.why5: It keeps what I typed: the super says the assignee while filming and Fresco drafts the notes, and checking them before they go out is the real habit my hallucination sceptics would care about.
screens.why7: Each row is a base-form verb phrase in 'their' voice, at most 9 words, and is a step the super takes themselves rather than a sign-off, a setup, Compatibility or Purchase friction; the count of 2 is within 1 to 4, and either row gives a belief that a Yes or an Only if could support and a Probably not or No could refute.

screens.why1: Right after I said what supers would have to do to start, picking the one effort most likely to stop them is the obvious next step.
screens.why2: Both rows read straight off on a jobsite: naming who's on each item and checking the notes before they go to the crew are things a super does every day, though 'owns' is a touch office-speak next to 'who's on it'.
screens.why3: Both are the super's own hands-on habits on the walk and after it, and a super knows at once whether they'd do them.
screens.why4: Two distinct efforts: one is on the walk, the other is reviewing the output after. Both are mine and neither is filler, so the list is complete for what I typed.
screens.why5: My core ask was taking short videos and talking over them on the walk; the list now leads with only the assignee part of that narration, which keeps my mechanism but narrows it, probably to stay clear of Compatibility's talking-over-the-noise row.
screens.why7: Each row is a step the super takes themselves, in base form and the 'they' voice, with no sign-off and nothing the product does. Neither repeats Compatibility or Purchase friction, and the belief 'Most would name who owns each item as they film' can be supported or refuted on the yes/only-if/probably-not/no scale with I can't tell apart.
screens.instead: Which one is most likely to stop them? Say who's on each item as they film · Check and fix the notes before they go out to the crew

screens.why1: Right before the study goes out is the obvious point to decide whether to collect emails from supers who'd try it, and nothing earlier asked this.
screens.why2: 'Pilot' is my own word, since I sell paid pilots on one site, and the hint spells out exactly what respondents will see.
screens.why3: Whether I want leads from superintendents is my call to make, and I know I do because supers are how I get in the door at a GC.
screens.why4: Yes or no covers it, the two options are distinct, and neither is odd.
screens.why5: The respondent line 'Would you try this for real? Leave your email.' names no product, price or buyer role, so nothing of mine leaks and my 'Yes' is kept.

screens.why1: Picking the interviewer voice right before launch is the obvious place for it, after the pilot offer and before people see the study.
screens.why2: Clear enough, though 400 credits and the record-once detail need a second read, and I typed lock and record the face while the screen offers voices, not faces.
screens.why3: As the founder I can judge which voice my supers would sit through on a text link after a long day.
screens.why4: Two named voices, each with a 5 second sample, Daphne preselected, and the same cost either way; nothing missing or overlapping for a choice like this.
screens.why5: Nothing of my product or roles is touched here, and the hint keeps the text-message link that suits supers in the field.
screens.instead: Say whether it is a face or only a voice being recorded, and that supers can read and tap instead of talking over site noise.

screens.why1: After choosing who asks the questions, picking how superintendents answer is the obvious next step before sending.
screens.why2: Plain words; 'AI interviewer', 'read and tap' and 'link' are clear to me as a founder building an AI product.
screens.why3: I know my supers are on phones in noisy sites and trailers, so I can judge which format they'd actually finish.
screens.why4: Three distinct options covering AI, text, and respondent's choice, with no overlap or missing case.
screens.why5: Nothing of Fresco's product or roles leaks; it's a delivery choice and my pick of Read and tap is kept.

screens.why1: After choosing how supers answer, deciding who gets a link is the natural last step before sending interviews.
screens.why2: Plain words; 'Contacts page' and 'open link' are Keel's own UI and clear in context, and signing in with Google is familiar.
screens.why3: I know whether I'm sending to supers I've met on jobs around the Bay or posting in a group, so I can answer from what I actually do.
screens.why4: The three ways (named people, a Keel search list, one open link in a group) are distinct and cover how I'd reach supers, and no escape is needed for a routing choice.
screens.why5: Nothing of Fresco's product or roles leaks here and my pick of people I know by name is kept as typed.

screens.why_b1: The verdict 'Too few to call' sits under the title with its deciding number beside it ('Compatibility: 4 counted'), and each card repeats '4 counted · 5 needed to call it'.
screens.why_b2: Counted against needed is plain on every card, but the page says 7 answered and only 4 counted without saying why the other 3 dropped out, so I had to look twice.
screens.why_b3: The three dimension names and beliefs are recognisably mine (talking into the phone over site noise, naming who owns each item as they film), but the statement repeats its outputs ('turns them into notes… and gets back notes…') and the relative-advantage line is tangled grammar.
screens.why_b4: '5 needed to call it' implies I need at least one more counted answer per belief, but the page never says so or tells me what to do: send to more supers, or open the cards to see who wasn't counted.
screens.why_b5: Nothing is claimed beyond the data: n is visible, the low count is named as too few on every card, and no belief is called held or failed.
screens.instead: Too few to call: 4 of the 7 supers who answered counted on each belief and 5 are needed, because 3 didn't fit [reason]. Send the study to at least 2 more superintendents before reading anything into the solution.

screens.why_b1: The verdict 'Too few to call' sits right beside '4 counted · 5 needed to call it', so I know both the call and the number behind it.
screens.why_b2: The bars plainly count 3 for and 1 against over 4 people, but the strip's 'your bar · 4 of 5' sits next to '5 needed' and the '1 in 3' rule, so I have to stop and work out whether 4 of 5 is the threshold or the count.
screens.why_b3: The belief is my row from revision 25, though 'on commercial jobs' is dropped, and the question asks about my 'last daily log' when I moved the occasion to the site walk, which is where the noise actually is.
screens.why_b4: 'Ray's no is the one to ask about' gives me one concrete step, but the card never says that one more answer decides this, or what a fail here would mean for filming on the walk.
screens.why_b5: n and 'a lean, not a call' stay visible, but the 'One more thing' quote filed under Compatibility is about the schedule slipping, not about talking over the noise, so it reads as evidence on a question it doesn't answer.
screens.instead: Ask about their last site walk; 3 of 4 could talk over the noise and 1 couldn't, so one more answer calls it; ask Ray what drowned him out.

screens.why_b1: The status 'Too few to call' sits right beside '4 counted · 5 needed to call it', so I know why there's no verdict: one answer short of the floor.
screens.why_b2: The chart is clear that 3 said a lot better and 1 said no difference out of 4, but the strip's 'your bar · 4 of 5' reads like a pass mark of four for-answers out of five, which clashes with 'no more than 1 in 3 say no difference or worse', and I had to work out that the ghost cell is Luis.
screens.why_b3: The belief line carries both of my benefits in my words, hours back at the end of the day and action items to the crew the same day, against the trailer-upload day I described, though the bar line only echoes the first.
screens.why_b4: 'Nothing is settled here yet' is generic; it doesn't tell me that one more counted superintendent would settle it, or that Denise, who finishes her log on the tablet before the gate, is the kind of super this doesn't help.
screens.why_b5: It hedges properly ('a lean, not a call') but the count line says the question was about 'their last daily log' when it asked about the last trailer-upload day, and 'your bar · 4 of 5' implies a threshold the rule line doesn't state.
screens.instead: Too few to call: 3 of 4 counted said a lot better and 1 said no difference (Denise, whose log is done on site). One more counted super decides it, and if that super also says no difference it won't hold.

screens.why_b1: The verdict 'Too few to call' sits right beside its deciding number, '4 counted · 5 needed to call it', and the So line repeats both, so I know where I stand and why.
screens.why_b2: The bars plainly count 5 supers' answers (3 for, 1 against), but the strip's 'your bar · 4 of 5' with the marker at 4 mixes up the 5-person floor and the 1-in-3 bar, and the bar line just repeats my belief, so I had to look twice to see where the bar sits.
screens.why_b3: 'Adoption friction' and 'Most would name who owns each item as they film' are my words, the step I picked, and the stranger's question asks exactly that.
screens.why_b4: 'Nothing is settled here yet' is generic: it doesn't say that one more counted super would settle it, that the lean is 3 for and 1 against, or that two of my three yeses hang on it not slowing the walk, which is the design constraint I'd act on.
screens.why_b5: n stays visible (5 answered, 4 counted), Luis's guess is set aside and named, the small group is called 'a lean, not a call', and nothing claims the belief held.
screens.instead: Too few to call: 4 of 5 counted, 3 for and 1 against, so it leans toward holding; two of the yeses hinge on it keeping the walk moving, so naming owners has to cost seconds, not stops. One more counted super settles it.

screens.why_b1: Each box opens on 'Too few to call' with '4 counted · 5 needed to call it' right beside it, so I know there is no answer yet and exactly why.
screens.why_b3: The dimension names and the Compatibility line ('could talk into their phone over the noise on site') are mine, but the Relative advantage line is mangled into 'their last day when they stayed in the trailer uploading photos would have given them hours back': recognisable, but not how I put it.
screens.why_b4: Nothing says what to do with one 'against' per line out of four counted, such as getting more supers to answer or the fact that both no's point at schedule and subs rather than the log.
screens.why_b5: The n is shown on every box, the low count is named as 'too few to call', and no line claims more than the single quote under it can carry.
screens.why_b6: Ray's 'the log can wait till morning, the deck can't' and Denise's tablet log done before the gate both tell me something I did not type: the real squeeze is the schedule and subs, and some supers already close the log on site.

screens.why1: Asking first whether my jobs run their daily logs in a system like Procore makes sense as the gate before anything else, though the 'A recent time' kicker doesn't really fit a yes-or-no about how my jobs are set up.
screens.why2: I'd answer it straight off, but nobody on site says 'construction project management system'; we say Procore or ACC, so naming those would land quicker.
screens.why3: I know exactly where my daily logs go on every job I run.
screens.why4: Yes or No covers it cleanly for a gate, and no escape is needed here.
screens.why5: It keeps the founder's Procore-or-ACC daily-log segment without leaking anything about their product or their own terms for me.
screens.why6: It's one short question with two options I can hold, but 'construction project management system' is a long run of words to hear once.
screens.instead: Do any of the jobs you run keep their daily logs in Procore, ACC or a system like them? Yes / No

screens.why1: Right after asking whether my jobs keep daily logs in a system like Procore, asking whether I sent one in short on photos this week is the obvious next step.
screens.why2: Daily log and site photos are my everyday words, and I can answer on first hearing, though I would wonder for a second whether a few photos missing counts or only none at all.
screens.why3: I submit the log every day, so I know whether I pushed one through without the walk photos attached this week.
screens.why4: Yes or No covers it, and the chips belong to the story box after a Yes, so they are no fault of the gate.
screens.why5: Nothing about a product or the company's plan reaches me; it asks about a log I sent, in words I would use.
screens.why6: One short question with Yes or no at the end, easy to hear once and answer.
screens.why7: Two fixed answers with no escape, and both are true of someone: a super who got the photos in says No and one who sent the log without them says Yes, so the belief can be held or refuted.

screens.why1: Part 1 asked me about my daily logs and photos, so showing me the idea before Part 2 is the obvious next step.
screens.why2: Site walk, crew, action items, Procore and ACC are all my own words; 'assignees' is a bit office-speak, but I'd get it straight off.
screens.why3: I walk the site every day, take photos and short videos, and push notes into Procore, so I can picture this on my own job.
screens.why4: It's a card to read, with no options.
screens.why5: Part 1 was all about the daily log, but the card never says the notes become my daily log, and 'would give you all of that' doesn't say what I'd actually get, like hours back each night or a cleaner record for a delay dispute.
screens.why6: Three short sentences that say fine out loud, and ACC is a name every super on Autodesk says as letters anyway.
screens.instead: Imagine Fresco, an AI scribe that writes up what you film and say. During the site walk you take short videos and talk over them; it turns them into the day's log with photos, who's on what and when it's due, texts the crew their items, and sends it to Procore or ACC in one click. The people building it believe it would save you the hours of uploading at the end of the day.

screens.why1: Right after the idea card, it makes sense to ask whether I could even talk into my phone out on site, since the whole thing depends on that.
screens.why2: The words are plain, but tying it to my last daily log is off, because I write the log in the trailer at the end of the day and the talking would happen on the walk, so I had to read it twice.
screens.why3: I know exactly how loud it gets with saws, compressors and the excavator running, and whether I could have been heard on my phone.
screens.why4: Easily, most of the time, only sometimes, no covers it, and I can't tell fits as the escape.
screens.why5: The only product words are on the idea card shown on purpose, and the question itself talks about my phone and the noise in my words.
screens.why6: It is short, one question, and four short options I can hold after hearing them once.
screens.why7: This is an ability row with the four ability options in order and the I can't tell escape, and noise on site is true for some days and jobs and not others, so it could go either way.
screens.instead: Think of your last site walk. Could you have talked into your phone over the noise on site? Yes, easily; yes, most of the time; only sometimes; no; or I can't tell.

screens.why1: Right after the idea card and the noise question, it makes sense to ask whether this thing would have beaten how I do my logs today.
screens.why2: Every word is mine, but 'helped you keep an accurate record of the day's work on site better' reads clumsily, and I had to read it twice to see that 'better' goes with keeping the record.
screens.why3: I know those days in the trailer after the walk, uploading photos and typing the log, so I can answer from my own week.
screens.why4: The four options are distinct and cover how I would actually answer, from a lot better to worse, and 'I can't tell' fits as the way out.
screens.why5: Nothing of the product leaks past the card, and the trailer line sounds like me, but the moment drifted from part 1's problem, which was a log that went in missing site photos, to an ordinary long day of uploading.
screens.why6: It says fine as a list of four plus the way out, but the stem runs about thirty words and 'keep an accurate record of the day's work on site better, or not' is a mouthful to hear once.
screens.why7: The measure, the four fixed options and the escape all meet the card, but the hard case is the routine trailer day rather than the moment it went wrong (the log missing photos), and that day's cost is my time, not accuracy, so a super whose log was right but took hours would say 'No difference' and the answer would not test the belief.
screens.instead: Think of the last daily log you sent in missing site photos. Would it have helped you keep an accurate record of that day better, or not? A lot better · A little better · No difference · Worse · I can't tell

screens.why1: After asking whether Fresco would help, it makes sense to ask whether I'd take on the extra step it needs while I'm walking.
screens.why2: On a job site 'owns' makes me think of the owner, the client, so I'd stop and reread it before I got to 'which sub or foreman is on it', and 'each item' doesn't say whether it means punch items, issues or every photo.
screens.why3: I know which sub is on what as I walk, so I can say straight off whether I'd call that out on camera.
screens.why4: Yes, a real condition, probably not and no cover it, and 'keeps the site walk moving' is exactly my catch, because I won't stop every ten feet to dictate.
screens.why5: 'Name who owns each item' sounds like office action-item talk, not how a super says it, so the founder's own wording shows through a little.
screens.why6: It is short and is one question with four short options and one escape, so it's easy to hold when heard once.
screens.why7: It's a step of use I'd take myself, the options are the fixed four in order, two for and two against, the condition is mine and not true of every step, and 'I can't tell' is there as the escape.
screens.instead: To use Fresco, you'd say which sub is responsible for each issue as you film. Would you do that, or not? Yes · Only if it keeps the site walk moving · Probably not · No · I can't tell

typo_leaks.text: How far back should construction superintendents look for the last time the day's site walks are done and the photoss and notes still have to go into the dailyy log?
